hero.headline: Reconstructing what happened, from what was left behind.
hero.lede: Khalad — digital forensics and incident response. I trace intrusions through registry hives, file system metadata, and log artifacts until the story holds together.

paragraphs: I'm a cybersecurity graduate specializing in digital forensics and incident response. My work centers on Windows artifact analysis — registry, MFT, USN Journal, Prefetch, and log correlation — to reconstruct how a system was compromised and what an intruder actually did.
I completed a DFIR-focused internship at a government entity, and I learn best by working real cases rather than studying theory in isolation — most of what's below came out of that approach.

project.title: ForensiQ + EZ Toolkit
paragraphs: An automated DFIR web platform (ForensiQ) paired with a desktop forensics toolkit (EZ Toolkit) that runs Windows artifact analysis end to end — registry, event logs, MFT, and browser history — instead of chaining separate tools by hand.
The desktop toolkit is a Python app that wraps Eric Zimmermann's tool suite in a working interface, handling tool paths and output parsing so the analyst gets straight to the findings.

cases.title: Dropper behavior analysis via reverse engineering
cases.description: Decompiled a dropper sample in Cutter and confirmed its two-branch execution logic: on success, it delays via ping before executing the dropped payload with ShellExecuteW; on failure, it self-deletes with a cmd.exe call. Correlated it to a related sample from the same investigation.

cases.title: Live investigation — Worm.Ramnit intrusion
cases.description: Investigated a compromised machine live, identifying Worm.Ramnit through VirusTotal and correlating Prefetch, AppData, and jumplist artifacts to build a timeline of execution and persistence.

cases.title: Cobalt Strike intrusion chain reconstruction
cases.description: Traced a Cobalt Strike–related intrusion chain by correlating Windows Defender, PowerShell, and Sysmon logs into a single sequence of attacker activity.

cases.title: Data exfiltration — USN Journal & MFT analysis
cases.description: Reconstructed a data exfiltration scenario using USN Journal and MFT analysis, including identifying a decoy flag deliberately planted in the Journal to mislead the investigation.

cases.title: BitLocker recovery via GPP cpassword decryption
cases.description: Recovered access to a BitLocker-encrypted drive by exploiting the Group Policy Preferences cpassword vulnerability (MS14-025) to decrypt stored credentials.
